assign.request: make the notes pages use 50% for image, 50% for prose, make the image sticky
assign.now: scoping - read note.js, notes.css, readme.md, two note pages, Page.class.js, Page.css grid
steps: design the split (CSS-only, scoped via :has(> .notes-shot), gated by a min-width floor)
edit note.js (drop now-inert wide class, keep everything else)

log.msg: usage.json refresh skipped - not in this task's write fence (public/notes/note.js, notes.css, readme.md line, task dir only); mastermind keeps the snapshot current.

layout skill, five questions. 1 container: .page's own grid (note pages are ROOT pages, not columns/catalog hosts) - the split spans the WHOLE main+wide region, not just main. 2 size: two 1fr columns between the page's gutters, each roughly half the page width; below ~900px total the left column would be under ~400px and the photo stops being legible, so it stacks to one column instead. 3 own layout: left = the existing .notes-shot figure (flex v v-center gap), now sticky; right = whatever content() drew after it (crumbs, .md blocks), each capped to --measure and left-aligned - centering would ragged-edge headings/lists/code in a half that is much wider than one measure at 3440. 4 regions: two (photo, prose), both inside the one page grid - no nested child pages. 5 preview: unchanged, out of scope (page.js not touched).

design: no JS restructuring. note.js's shot() already marks the figure .notes-shot, so notes.css scopes the split with .page:has(> .notes-shot) inside @media (min-width: 900px) only - below that width every existing rule is untouched (today's already-shipped single-column stack: photo full width, then measure-capped prose). Above it: notes-shot gets grid-column:left, grid-row:1/-1, position:sticky, top:var(--pad-y) (the page's own top padding token); every other direct child gets grid-column:right, and gets max-width:var(--measure) unless it says .wide/.bleed (the sitewide opt-out convention) - so a page's own full-width wall still renders, just confined to the right half's width, not the old full page-wide breakout. notes.css is @layer site, which beats Page.css's @layer theme unconditionally regardless of specificity, so no !important or selector arms race is needed.

Dead end, logged not hidden: a CSS-Grid version (.notes-shot grid-row:1/-1 beside auto-placed siblings, scoped :has(> .notes-shot)) measured row1 inflated to the spanning items full height - a 51px h1 sat in a 467px row with a few hundred px of blank space before the crumb bar, on layouts-need-fit at 1280. Replaced with float + display:flow-root (classic sticky-sidebar technique, no grid at all): .notes-shot floats left at 50% - gap/2 and is position:sticky; everything else gets margin-left to clear it. No row-sizing ambiguity, verified by rect measurement (h1 back to its own ~50px).

Pages that fight the split (found, not edited, per the brief): layouts-need-fit/page.js sketch_wall() and scale-1920-to-3413/page.js calculator() both mark themselves .wide to break out to the pages old full wide track; under the split .wide still lands in the right half (so it still works) but is confined to about half the width it used to get. scale-1920-to-3413/page.js also does not use NotesNote at all - it hand-builds its own figure.c(notes-shot ...) - which is exactly why the split had to be a pure CSS rule keyed off the .notes-shot class, never a note.js render() override: a JS-side fix would have missed this page entirely.

Verified headless (Playwright) on layouts-need-fit, scale-1920-to-3413, and doodles at 400/900/1280/1920/3440: zero console errors and zero sideways scroll at every width on every page. Split (position:sticky) holds from 900 up - shotWidth 407px at 900, just over the ~400px legibility floor; stacks (position:static, unchanged pre-task behaviour) at 400. doodles has no .notes-shot and renders exactly as before - the rule never fires on it. 800px-scroll sticky proof at 1280 on both real note pages: the photo rect is identical before and after scrolling and fully within the viewport both times. Screenshots (5 widths x 3 pages + 2 scroll-proof shots) and probe-results.json are in this task dir.

assign.outcome:
**A note page is now half photo, half prose, side by side, and the photo stays put.** Above a 900px floor `notes.css` splits a note page 50/50: the picture floats left and is `position: sticky` (it rides along while the right side scrolls under it); everything else lands in the right half, left-aligned, capped to the page's own reading measure. Below 900px it falls back to the plain stack it already had (photo full width, then prose, nothing sticky) - untouched. The whole thing is one CSS rule keyed off the `.notes-shot` class (`:has(> .notes-shot)`), so it works on every note automatically, including one that never imports `NotesNote`. Verified headless at 400/900/1280/1920/3440 on both note pages plus `doodles`: zero console errors, zero sideways scroll anywhere, sticky confirmed with an 800px scroll test at 1280 on both pages.
